rules.statement: Don't map every caught InvalidOperationException (or other broad exception) from a store to 409 Conflict; detect the conflict from already-loaded state before calling external services or the store, and let other store failures propagate.
rules.why: A broad catch turns unrelated store failures into a misleading duplicate-identifier 409, hides the real cause, and can trigger compensating actions such as destroying a newly created external key.
rules.check: Look for catch blocks around store add/save calls that return 409 for a general exception type, and for conflict checks done only after side-effecting external calls.

rules.statement: Declare every error status a minimal API route can answer with .ProducesProblem (including 401/403 unless a group-level declaration covers them), not just the success response.
rules.why: Undeclared responses are missing from the OpenAPI document, so generated clients and consumers of the contract can't see them.
rules.check: For new or changed endpoint mappings, compare the statuses the handler returns or documents against the .Produces/.ProducesProblem declarations on the route and its group.

rules.statement: Make a code comment state only what the adjacent code enforces or does, not effects that happen elsewhere.
rules.why: A comment claiming an effect the code doesn't have leads maintainers to rely on the check for the wrong thing or to remove it.
rules.check: Compare each new comment's claims with the behavior of the method it sits in.

rules.statement: When validation rejects a value that isn't one of a known registered set, include the accepted values (ordinally sorted, or a note that none are registered) in the error detail.
rules.why: A caller who mistypes a name otherwise gets a 400 with no hint and has to look elsewhere for the valid names.
rules.check: Look for validation errors for unknown names/algorithms/providers that don't list the valid options.

rules.statement: When two handlers end with the same sequence of steps (build resource, audit, notify, set ETag, return result), extract that sequence into one private method both call.
rules.why: Duplicated copies drift, for example when only one gets a changed audit or notification step.
rules.check: Look for identical multi-step tails in sibling handler methods added in the diff.

rules.statement: In a test project, cover each failure branch (not found, validation failure, conflict) for every route that has them, matching the coverage given to sibling routes.
rules.why: A regression in an untested branch passes the unit tests.
rules.check: Compare the failure-branch tests of sibling routes and flag a route missing tests for branches it shares with another.

rules.statement: In a test project, when a method returns the same status for several causes, assert the specific error detail in each test, not only the status code.
rules.why: Otherwise a test can pass because a different check refused the input than the one it names.
rules.check: Look for failure tests that assert only a status code where the code under test has multiple refusals with that status.

rules.statement: In a test project, build fixture inputs that are valid for the real contract even when the collaborator that would reject them is mocked.
rules.why: An invalid value that passes only because of a mock suggests to readers that it is a valid input.
rules.check: Look for request fixtures using values (formats, encodings, enum members) the real API doesn't accept.

rules.statement: In a test project, derive timestamps from a fixed instant or the registered/fake TimeProvider, not DateTimeOffset.UtcNow or DateTime.UtcNow.
rules.why: Tests that read the wall clock depend on the real time and can become flaky.
rules.check: Search new test code for DateTimeOffset.UtcNow, DateTime.UtcNow or DateTime.Now.

rules.statement: When a decision record or document defers work as separate work, link the tracking issue.
rules.why: Deferred work without a tracked home can be forgotten.
rules.check: Look for 'separate work', 'later', 'future' or similar deferrals in docs/ADRs with no issue link.

rules.statement: When an API adds an input limit or refusal (maximum length, rejected characters), state it in the decision record and the capability documentation that describe that input.
rules.why: Readers can't otherwise tell that such inputs are refused.
rules.check: Compare new validation limits in the diff with the docs and ADR text describing that field.

rules.statement: Don't ask a Helm chart to fail rendering when a key management service provider has no workload credentials configured; a provider without them uses the pod's ambient identity, so only half-set or malformed credential settings are refused.
rules.why: The chart never requires KMS workload credentials, on any path; ambient identity (node role, managed identity, attached service account) is a supported configuration.
rules.check: Before reporting, check the chart README's credentials section and the existing render-time checks for whether missing credentials are documented as optional.
